subject: GLM-4.6: A Data-Driven Look at China's Rising AI Model
snippet: A Chinese AI model went from 168 million to 15.9 billion tokens in 12 days—a 94-fold explosion that nobody saw coming. ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏
body:
View this post on the web at https://blog.kilocode.ai/p/glm-46-a-data-driven-look-at-chinas

On September 29th, GLM-4.6 recorded 168 million tokens on Kilo Code’s leaderboard [ https://substack.com/redirect/608483d1-9f1f-4751-b22f-561b50d9f576?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]. Twelve days later: 15.9 billion tokens. That’s one of the fastest adoption curves we’ve seen for any open source / open weights language model.
Why it matters: GLM-4.6 from Zhipu AI just proved you can build frontier AI without NVIDIA chips, charge 2% of Western prices, and still rank fourth globally. The AI market isn’t what we thought it was.
Background: Zhipu AI and the Hardware Challenge
Zhipu AI [ https://substack.com/redirect/c6388c41-eb9d-49a7-95a0-a591058981b7?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ], now branded as Z.ai [ https://substack.com/redirect/611cdfce-fa3f-4092-8168-4a4b5a36ab30?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ], is a Tsinghua University spinoff founded in 2019, backed by Alibaba and Tencent. After U.S. export restrictions cut off access [ https://substack.com/redirect/37b8de5e-c595-4386-b00d-27c17a96be39?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] to NVIDIA GPUs earlier this year, Zhipu partnered with domestic chip manufacturers Cambricon and Moore Threads. GLM-4.6 runs on these Chinese-made accelerators using FP8/Int4 quantization, enabling the 357-billion parameter model to operate without Western hardware - likely contributing to their ability to offer the service at a fraction of competitors’ prices.
Performance Metrics and Benchmarks
According to the LMArena leaderboard [ https://substack.com/redirect/304ac88b-f3f8-4d30-9de5-6cfd35277482?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ], GLM-4.6 [ https://substack.com/redirect/92dc8997-2b1f-4e2e-92de-cae712045606?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] ranks fourth overall and first among open source models. In practical coding evaluations – 74 challenges run in a Claude Code environment - GLM-4.6 achieved a 48.6% win rate [ https://substack.com/redirect/92dc8997-2b1f-4e2e-92de-cae712045606?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] against Anthropic’s Claude Sonnet 4.
The model’s specifications include:
357 billion parameters in a Mixture-of-Experts architecture
200,000 token context window (approximately 400 pages of text)
MIT licensed open weights
15% improvement in token efficiency compared to GLM-4.5
Internal evaluations  [ https://substack.com/redirect/92dc8997-2b1f-4e2e-92de-cae712045606?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]show GLM-4.6 leading on benchmarks like AIME (mathematics) and BrowseComp (web browsing), while trailing Claude 4.5 on complex long-form reasoning tasks like τ²-Bench.
The Pricing Model
Zhipu’s GLM Coding Plan [ https://substack.com/redirect/1971e6a4-f35d-48b3-8189-16dddafc6029?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] starts at $3 USD per month for the Lite tier, increasing to $6 after the promotional period. The Pro tier runs $15 initially, $30 thereafter. For context, Anthropic’s Claude API charges approximately $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens. A moderate coding session can easily consume millions of tokens.
The subscription includes what Zhipu describes as “tens to hundreds of billions” of tokens monthly. Even at the standard rates, this represents a 50-100x cost reduction compared to leading Western API services.
What developers actually say
I analyzed discussions across Reddit’s AI communities. The pattern is clear:
The praise [ https://substack.com/redirect/6b7878bd-1e91-40c1-b82c-a204b4310884?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]:
“Far better than any open-source model in my testing”
Strong on structured coding tasks, especially frontend
Excellent logical reasoning and problem decomposition
Native bilingual support (Chinese/English)
The reality [ https://substack.com/redirect/b755f387-64ff-4c82-b030-c918d77ffdd0?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]:
Performance gap with Claude 4.5 on complex tasks
One developer [ https://substack.com/redirect/8367c4df-31d9-466d-8d9f-4b60641a7f67?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]: Claude Code finished a Unity game in 6 hours; GLM-4.6 struggled despite consuming millions of tokens
13% syntax error rate vs. 5.5% in GLM-4.5
Occasional language mixing in outputs
The pragmatic pattern: Developers use GLM-4.6 for routine coding (80% of work), reserve premium models for complex debugging.
The deeper story
This isn’t about GLM-4.6 being “better” than Claude or GPT-5. It’s about market segmentation that is a brand new one that we haven’t seen before.
Turns out there’s massive demand for “good enough” AI at commodity prices. If 80% of coding tasks can be handled by a model costing 2% of premium alternatives, the economics become compelling.
What this means: The market is moving toward commoditization faster than anyone anticipated. Not because of technical breakthroughs, but because alternative development paths bypass traditional constraints.
The stakes: This signals a new phase in AI development. Competitive models from Chinese labs, running on domestic hardware, offered at prices that undercut Western providers by orders of magnitude.
What’s next
The 94-fold growth in 12 days isn’t just adoption—it’s validation. Developers are voting with their API calls that accessibility and cost-effectiveness matter as much as raw capability.
Action steps for developers:
Test GLM-4.6 for routine coding tasks
Keep premium models for complex reasoning
Download the open weights if you need data sovereignty
Watch the pricing—promotional rates end eventually
Action steps for companies:
Recognize the “good enough” AI market is real
Budget-conscious teams have viable alternatives now
Hardware independence matters for long-term strategy
The AI duopoly just became a competitive market
The bottom line: We’re watching the democratization of AI capabilities in real-time. GLM-4.6 delivers 80-90% of frontier capability at a fraction of the cost. For many use cases, that trade-off is acceptable.
The question isn’t whether this changes the market. The Kilo Code data already answered that. The question is what happens when the next model does this even better.

body:
View this post on the web at https://blog.kilocode.ai/p/every-engineering-managers-ai-dilemma

Your developers are using AI. That’s not changing. The only question is whether you’re giving them a sanctioned, secure way to do it—or watching it happen in the shadows until something breaks.
The BYOAI era isn’t coming. It’s here. And every day you spend deciding whether to engage with that reality is another day someone else gets ahead.
Every engineering leader I talk to is hearing the same thing from their CEO: “Our competitors are using AI. We need an AI strategy. Figure it out.” The manager nods, walks back to their desk, and realizes they have absolutely no idea how to actually do this well and safely.
Developers Already Chose AI
While leadership debates AI strategy, tech workers already made the decision—they’re using AI tools with personal accounts and expense-reported subscriptions.
Why it matters: This isn’t a gap between adoption and readiness. It’s a chasm. Only 13% of companies feel ready to capture value from generative AI, but developers aren’t waiting for permission.
Reality check: Your developers aren’t being reckless. They’re watching peers at other companies ship features in hours that used to take days. Controlled studies show developers complete tasks 55% faster with AI assistance. The productivity gains are real, so they find workarounds.
The deeper story: Developers sanitize code snippets “just enough” before pasting them into ChatGPT. They debate in Slack whether their API schema counts as “proprietary.” They convince themselves that one small function couldn’t possibly matter.
By the numbers:
90% of tech workers use AI on the job [ https://substack.com/redirect/11a788f1-b134-424a-8e57-9006d25eb628?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]
13% of companies feel ready for generative AI [ https://substack.com/redirect/595cd0ce-39bc-4764-bbeb-531b7835d0ca?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]
55% faster task completion with AI assistance [ https://substack.com/redirect/4f63151c-32ca-43a2-97ea-a7cc65bfab13?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]
The stakes: Every unsanctioned ChatGPT session is proprietary code in an unknown training pipeline. Every personal Copilot subscription is a security audit waiting to happen. Every “just this once” workaround becomes standard practice.
What’s next: Stop debating adoption. Start channeling it. Give your team transparent, secure AI tools with clear boundaries, or watch it happen in the shadows with zero visibility and maximum risk.
Why the Standard Playbook Fails
Most engineering leaders I talk to are stuck in analysis paralysis. They see two options, and both look terrible:
1️⃣ Build internal tooling. Spin up an AI infrastructure team. Hire ML engineers (good luck—they’re the most competitive hire in tech). Set up GPU clusters. Build observability. Manage model updates. Create an internal developer platform. Maintain it forever while the AI landscape shifts every quarter.
2️⃣ Buy a black box. Sign up for GitHub Copilot, Cursor, or whoever has the slickest demo. Accept opaque pricing with “fair use” clauses you don’t understand. Watch rate limits appear mysteriously during crunch time. Get invoiced for five figures because you crossed some invisible threshold the vendor won’t explain until after the fact.
One developer recently described Cursor’s pricing as “bait-and-switch”—promising unlimited usage that quietly degraded once they were locked in.
Both approaches miss what’s actually possible: your developers get the AI superpowers they’re already using in secret, and you get the security, cost control, and visibility you need to sleep at night.
The Mental Model That Works
The best teams I’ve seen have landed on the same mental model: treat AI like a very fast, energetic junior developer.
Smart. Enthusiastic. Has read every public repo and technical textbook. Outputs code at lightning speed.
BUT also: zero context about your specific project. Needs explicit instructions. Makes confident mistakes. Requires code review like everyone else.
This framing solves most of the “AI strategy” problem. You don’t need a special governance framework for AI. You need the same framework you use for junior developers:
The difference is this junior developer works at 50-120 tokens per second and never needs coffee breaks.
What Engineering Leaders Actually Need to Provide
Once you adopt the ‘very fast junior developer’ mental model, the path out of the engineering manager’s dilemma becomes clear:
📊 Real visibility into usage
Track your AI junior like any team member. See which models tackle which tasks. Know what works. Skip the aggregated dashboards—you need actual data. You wouldn’t let a junior work in isolation. Don’t do it with AI.
🚦 Guardrails, not gates
Junior developers need freedom within boundaries. So does AI.
Approved model lists (like library access for juniors)
Clear data-sharing policies (the “don’t push to main” equivalent)
Automatic sensitive-data flagging (proactive code review)
🔄 Model flexibility
The best model changes monthly. Claude drops Sonnet 4.5. OpenAI ships o3. Some open-source model dominates overnight. Your AI junior needs the latest tools—without forcing everyone to learn new interfaces.
💰 Cost transparency
You know what juniors cost: salary, benefits, equipment. AI should be equally transparent. Forget “500 AI credits.” Show actual per-model costs. If Claude Opus costs more but needs less review, maybe it’s worth it—like paying extra for a junior who needs less mentoring.
Starting From Yes, Actually
Shopify’s approach [ https://substack.com/redirect/115461a3-142b-433b-9676-f7e093b4f1d6?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] is right: “Start from yes.” Assume AI will accelerate your team. Work backward to make it safe.
But what does that actually look like in practice?
Acknowledge reality. Your team is already using AI. The conversation isn’t “should we allow this?” It’s “how do we make this work?”
Provide sanctioned tools. Give developers an approved way to use AI that meets security requirements. If the alternative is random personal accounts, you’ve already lost. Just make sure those tools come with what you need - SSO, SCIM, and other security requirements.
Create clear policies, not permission structures. Don’t make people ask before using AI. Give them guidelines on what’s allowed and trust them to follow it. Treat exceptions as opportunities to update guidelines, not punish individuals.
Measure outcomes, not activity. Track whether AI usage correlates with faster shipping, fewer bugs, better documentation. Not whether people are “using it right.”
Invest in AI literacy. The developers who get the most from AI aren’t the ones who use it most. They’re the ones who use it best—knowing when to trust it, when to question it, and how to structure prompts for useful results.
The Choice You’re Actually Making
The problem isn’t whether to adopt AI for software development. That decision has already been made [ https://substack.com/redirect/1ab82284-2e6f-424e-8c85-d18fde1cefa8?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]—by your developers, whether you sanctioned it or not. The real question is how to enable AI adoption in a way that doesn’t create more problems than it solves.

body:
View this post on the web at https://blog.kilocode.ai/p/code-supernova-1m-context-window

TL;DR: Code Supernova upgraded today (Sept 26) to a massive 1 million token context window putting it in the same league as the other top tier models out there like OpenAI’s GPT4.1 and Anthropic’s Claude Sonnet 4. Most important of all, it’s still completely free through Kilo Code [ https://substack.com/redirect/ab07d70c-9875-4440-8cbd-0c60233afc70?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]; our 100% free, open source AI agent extension for VS Code [ https://substack.com/redirect/1ae7e5dc-9b5b-438f-9c3b-54d62cd07129?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] and JetBrains [ https://substack.com/redirect/ec6456ef-30ca-4f8b-a051-f86ecfc64eb5?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] with over 420,000 installs.
How It Started
When we first launched Code Supernova [ https://substack.com/redirect/76fbe3d7-530d-4a42-abc2-848c0689d8b4?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] in stealth last week (Sept 19) it packed impressive multimodal capabilities into just a 200K context window. Today, they’re taking it to the next level.
In your settings, `code-supernova` will be listed as `code-supernova-1-million` and you’ll be able to test out the difference immediately!
Why It Matters
For folks who don’t know what context window means in this context (😏); you can think of it as your model’s “attention span”. The phrase “working memory” is also used quite often to describe this but it’s essentially just how much information your model can keep in mind while helping you code. A larger context window means you can share more files, longer conversations, and bigger projects without the AI forgetting what you talked about earlier.
It’s almost like having RAM in the cloud, which makes my pranks in college where I convinced my friends that they could download RAM online a little ironic!
So like I mentioned above, a 1 million token context window puts Code Supernova in elite company. For comparison:
GPT4.1: 1M tokens ($15/million tokens)
Claude Sonnet 4: 1M tokens ($15/million tokens)
Gemini 2.5 Pro: 1M tokens ($7/million tokens)
Code Supernova: 1M tokens ($0 through Kilo Code)
With Code Supernova, you now can:
Upload entire codebases (8+ copies of the full React repo!)
Add screenshots to those codebases for additional context
Ship a full product starting with just a design mockup or architecture diagram!
What You Should Do

body:
View this post on the web at https://blog.kilocode.ai/p/announcing-kilo-for-enterprise

Right now, your developers are copying code into ChatGPT. They’re signing up for Claude with personal accounts. They’re using GitHub Copilot on their own dime. This isn’t a prediction—it’s what’s happening today [ https://substack.com/redirect/b190324f-b019-4928-8bcd-651d4a04fadc?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] in virtually every engineering organization.
The BYOAI (Bring Your Own AI [ https://substack.com/redirect/1bb511d8-8ae4-4524-b791-7936af3d5c98?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]) problem isn’t coming. It’s here.
Developers aren’t malicious. They’re pragmatic. AI coding tools make them 25% more productive [ https://substack.com/redirect/251f0016-80e8-4eb2-b82c-c6f5e10a7409?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] and 50% faster [ https://substack.com/redirect/9393beb2-50a8-4314-91b9-292592cfc184?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] than before, so they’ll find a way to use them. The question isn’t whether your team will adopt AI. It’s whether they’ll do it in a way that keeps your code secure and your company compliant.
That’s why we’re launching Kilo for Enterprise: the AI coding platform built for how enterprises actually work. Complete transparency. Total control. No compromises.
Your Data. Your Rules.
Here’s what makes Kilo for Enterprise different: transparency without compromise.
While GitHub Copilot gives you a black box and Cursor keeps their pricing behind a sales call, we give you exactly what enterprises need: complete visibility and control. You can see our source code [ https://substack.com/redirect/68db5619-2ab5-43ea-8cc9-332cf677c5e6?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]. You decide which models and providers your teams can use. Not only that, but you can select these from 500+ models [ https://substack.com/redirect/88bc355c-6146-4627-9ed4-46f6ce19dcd0?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] - including the very latest - you can also bring your own key to frontier lab providers via Bedrock or Vertex, and use self-hosted models.
Kilo for Enterprise is a complete platform for governing AI across your organization. Set model restrictions. Enforce usage policies. Know exactly how your data is processed. Get complete AI usage metrics broken down by user and model. Your security team gets the control they need while developers get the tools they want.
Pass Your Next Security Audit with Confidence
Every Enterprise customer gets:
Full SCIM provisioning and SSO/OIDC authentication
Complete audit logs for every interaction
SOC 2 compliance-ready architecture
Real SLAs for mission-critical development
Dedicated support channels with engineers who actually understand your needs
The audit logs and usage metrics aren’t just checkboxes for compliance. They give you real insights into how AI is being used across your organization. Which models are most effective for your codebase? Which teams are seeing the biggest productivity gains? Where are the bottlenecks? This is about optimization, not just oversight.
Open Source Core, Enterprise Scale
We’re built on open source because we believe you should never be locked into a vendor’s vision of AI. No vendor lock-in. No AI provider lock-in. Ever.
Unlike other tools, which require you to build enterprise features yourself, we’ve already done the hard work. You get the transparency and flexibility of open source with the support and scale of enterprise software. Deploy with confidence knowing you can always see what’s under the hood.
And unlike the black boxes of Copilot, Cursor, or others, our transparent architecture means you always know exactly how your code is being processed. Community-driven innovation keeps us honest and keeps you competitive.
Value-added agentic AI
This isn’t about features. It’s about transformation. It’s about turning AI from your biggest security risk into your biggest competitive advantage. It’s about keeping your IP inside your company and with AI inference providers you trust. You can even bring your own inference - that’s why we charge by the seat instead of creating a subscription to “AI credits,” “user messages,” or “premium requests.”
Compare it to the cost of a compliance failure. Or the cost of your best engineers leaving for companies that allow them to use the tools they need. Plus, with no markup on AI tokens and the ability to use free and stealth models, your team will get the best tool for the job, when they need it. No more waiting to ship a feature for my 5-hour rolling rate limit window to reset.
Built for All Your Stakeholders
For CTOs and Engineering Leaders: Deploy AI coding at scale without sacrificing security or control. Complete visibility into how your teams use AI, with granular controls over models, providers, and data handling.
For CISOs and Compliance Teams: Finally, an AI coding tool that speaks your language. Full audit logs, SSO integration, and the ability to restrict models mean you can enable innovation without enabling risk.
For CFOs and finance teams: Transparent pricing. No inference markup. Pay providers directly or use our simplified billing. One vendor relationship, complete flexibility. $299/user/month, no negotiation needed.
The Clock Is Ticking
Every day you wait is another day your developers are finding creative ways around your security policies. Another day your competitors who’ve figured this out are shipping faster. Another day of being asked, “What is our plan with AI?” Another day you’re accumulating risk you don’t even know about.
The choice isn’t whether to adopt AI for development. That decision has already been made by your developers. The choice is whether to do it right or pretend it’s not happening.
Kilo for Enterprise is available today. Schedule a demo [ https://substack.com/redirect/062df3c3-ed4a-4e18-8a95-401108bea9a7?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] with our team, and we’ll show you exactly how to make AI work for your enterprise—on your terms.
Because if you’re not planning your AI adoption, you’re planning for chaos. And chaos doesn’t scale.

Unsubscribe https://substack..VRyRqHhf4qfprPP0tNh-Bsm18CnHDHHTUje9uA15kkI?

am 3. November 2025 aktualisieren wir unsere Nutzungsbedingungen. Machen Sie sich mit den Änderungen vertraut. https://www.linkedin.com/e/v2?urlhash=miI9&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww%2Elinkedin%2Ecom%2Fhelp%2Flinkedin%2Fanswer%2Fa8059228&lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_comms_adhoc_2025_legal_tos_update_uk_eea%3B6P7hqt5lQWWeFKfLpsFSgQ%3D%3D&midToken=AQGZTB09IGnRcQ&midSig=3b3bsO841QbXY1&ek=email_comms_adhoc_2025_legal_tos_update_uk_eea&e=ops4wq-mfsra749-p0&eid=ops4wq-mfsra749-p0&m=email_body&ts=eml-comm_adhoc-uk-eea-tos_learn_more&li=0&t=plh

Dies kann Personalverantwortlichen helfen, Sie leichter zu finden und zu kontaktieren. Zudem werden Mitglieder bei der Erstellung von Inhalten wie Profil-Updates, Nachrichten und Beiträgen unterstützt. Dazu können Angaben in Ihrem Profil sowie öffentliche Inhalte zählen, die Sie auf LinkedIn erstellen. Ihre privaten Nachrichten sind davon nicht betroffen. Wenn Sie nicht möchten, dass Ihre Daten auf diese Weise verwendet werden, können Sie unter https://www.linkedin.com/e/v2?urlhash=KBj9&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww%2Elinkedin%2Ecom%2Fmypreferences%2Fd%2Fsettings%2Fdata-for-ai-improvement&lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_comms_adhoc_2025_legal_tos_update_uk_eea%3B6P7hqt5lQWWeFKfLpsFSgQ%3D%3D&midToken=AQGZTB09IGnRcQ&midSig=3b3bsO841QbXY1&ek=email_comms_adhoc_2025_legal_tos_update_uk_eea&e=ops4wq-mfsra749-p0&eid=ops4wq-mfsra749-p0&m=email_body&ts=eml-comm_adhoc-uk-eea-tos_opt_out&li=0&t=plh jederzeit die Opt-out-Option wählen. Kilo Code [ https://substack.com/redirect/acffdf7e-6d28-49c0-9e35-88451f91dd19?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] is a 100% free, open-source AI agent extension for VS Code [ https://substack.com/redirect/07e7cbac-3b5c-4727-b795-d6cc04b3a1c1?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] and JetBrains [ https://substack.com/redirect/4685f24a-166a-4457-8554-39c50616e84c?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] with over 420,000 installs.

A versatile agentic coding model that supports image inputs
Free for a limited time through our launch partnership
Users opt in to share usage data with the model provider to help improve the model.
Early access for Kilo Code users
200k context window (combined input/output)
Unlimited usage - no throttling, no caps
Check out this demo page [ https://substack.com/redirect/ed96b4f4-5735-4069-bdb3-8f0022f54dbc?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] that Code Supernova built for itself!
What Can You Do with Multimodal Input?

Understanding visual context: Interpret screenshots, diagrams and mockups alongside text. This helps the model to understand requirements when building, especially handy for frontend heavy projects.
Debugging with screenshots: Share screenshots of error messages, console outputs or unexpected UI behavior to get more accurate debugging help.
Design to code workflows: Add mockups, wireframes or even hand-drawn sketches and translate them into code.

subject: Kilo Code v4.92.0–v4.95.0: JetBrains Marketplace listing, auto-start a task, copy code blocks
body:
View this post on the web at https://blog.kilocode.ai/p/kilo-code-v4920v4950-jetbrains-marketplace

We’ve officially launched Kilo Code on the JetBrains Marketplace [ https://substack.com/redirect/df262bee-6aea-474a-875f-ac43d1ea4174?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]!
We also have several other cool new features for you. These notes cover 6 versions shipped over the last week (yes, we ship almost every day!)
Auto-start a task when launching VS Code
You can now auto-start a task when opening your VS Code workspace.
How to do it: Create a .kilocode directory in your project. Inside it, create a launchConfig.json and add JSON content to it. For example:
{
  "prompt": "Say hello world"
}
Now restart VS Code and see this in action! You can also configure your prompt to auto-run under different conditions.
Learn more: Read this document [ https://substack.com/redirect/18dbaf25-bdfd-4dbf-a71e-8eca7c69b0f6?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] for more advanced examples.
Contributor: hassoncs [ https://substack.com/redirect/734807ae-3249-457b-bccc-3a99f4a1ceb1?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] | Version: 4.95.0
More robust virtual provider
What’s new: The Kilo virtual provider now provides you a reason why it switches providers. It also automatically retries when it encounters a retriable error (429 or 503) instead of stopping.
What is a “virtual provider”?
It’s a feature introduced [ https://substack.com/redirect/2492f4eb-7e24-413c-8f41-c665281f3fd0?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] in v4.65.0.
It lets you seamlessly switch between models. You can learn more about using the virtual provider by clicking here. [ https://substack.com/redirect/1d78a88a-609e-409a-8593-3f096a0e6392?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]
Contributor: mcowger [ https://substack.com/redirect/684626e3-367d-429a-add4-dd2aa691d933?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] | Version: 4.94.0
Easily copy code blocks from the Kilo Code interface
For example: Let’s say you’re in Ask Mode and you ask Kilo to help you refactor a code file. You get certain recommendations with code snippets and you want the ability to easily copy those snippets.
You can now easily do that.
What changed: We added a toolbar next to a code snippet so you can easily copy the code snippets that Kilo provides to you:
Contributor: kevinvandijk [ https://substack.com/redirect/5aaf14a2-e297-4a82-ab9c-247177bf0c9b?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] | Version: v4.94.0
A better message when a model is no longer available
Kilo Code provides you access to hundreds fo AI models. Some of those models become unavailable after a certain period.
You should now get a friendly message instead of a confusing error whenever a model is no longer available:
Contributor: chrarnoldus [ https://substack.com/redirect/0816269c-11dd-49f2-a3fa-7f36a38952e4?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] | Version: v4.92.0
Other noteworthy updates
Autocomplete suggestions now support colorized code highlighting (thanks @hassoncs [ https://substack.com/redirect/abee7326-e89d-4501-be8c-3cddaae002da?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ], added in v4.95.0)
The default mode for new Kilo Code installations is now “Code Mode” (thanks @kevinvandijk [ https://substack.com/redirect/27b6f16b-a807-4726-8afd-e515c3243ece?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ], added in v4.94.0)
The Task History tab is now paginated (thanks @chrarnoldus [ https://substack.com/redirect/e0a32a5f-5503-4717-80eb-4c228c4f9aa3?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ], added in v4.95.0)
Improved light theme support for JetBrains IDEs (thanks @catrielmuller [ https://substack.com/redirect/761be8d6-4e4d-474c-8d11-703982387565?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ], added in v4.94.0)
Model updates

We fixed a context window issue with Ollama Turbo (thanks @chrarnoldus [ https://substack.com/redirect/b94c75b9-9cc9-43eb-b85d-9068cdf35ccf?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ], added in v4.93.0).

Two features, generating a commit message with AI and enhancing a prompt, now support billing through Kilo for Teams (thanks @chrarnoldus [ https://substack.com/redirect/25980b2b-1415-449e-8008-d1ba316b6cec?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ], added in v4.93.2)
The extension now enforces model restrictions set by your organization (thanks @charnoldus [ https://substack.com/redirect/412352cd-ba2f-4a1d-922f-4a3d68dcea40?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ], added in v4.93.1). You should see this screen if there’s a restriction:
Merged changes from Roo Code
Kilo Code v4.93.0 merged over 20 changes from Roo Code v3.26.5-v3.27.0. You can see the full list of changes here. [ https://substack.com/redirect/23343a2f-7add-456f-bb60-65a3ebf171c0?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]
We’re close to 10,000 GitHub stars!

body:
View this post on the web at https://blog.kilocode.ai/p/spc-vibe-coding-forum-with-kilo

Last Thursday, Kilo’s engineer Chris Hasson [ https://substack.com/redirect/10412028-3635-4faf-9c90-2ef50fe99c50?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] headed to South Park Commons [ https://substack.com/redirect/78a70a99-ded3-4cf4-a895-b55e7f93bf4a?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] (SPC) for their Vibe Coding Forum, led by John Bohannon [ https://substack.com/redirect/b1345faf-71c5-4f3e-831f-c7602034e1ec?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]. SPC isn't your typical tech meetup — it's a community of founders, highly-cited researchers, and first-time entrepreneurs all eager to build the next big thing.
Chris gave a quick recap of how Kilo Code came to be [ https://substack.com/redirect/ccb57ad3-f078-429d-8e19-f94255f1b878?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] and jumped straight into coding. The group voted to recreate a classic game: Snake. It started with a voice prompt:
“We’re in a brand-new repo and want to build an interactive snake game in TypeScript as a single-page app as quickly as possible... where you can use the arrow keys to move your snake around. You can eat apples in a 2D grid, and the snake should grow as it eats apples. Standard Snake rules.”
He flipped into Orchestrator mode [ https://substack.com/redirect/2cbacb38-31f5-41fc-af06-99bc978d39e5?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ], letting Kilo Code delegate tasks while the community watched it scaffold the project, initialize the Git repo, set up the build system, and start coding the core game structure in real-time.
While Kilo Code was taking on the code, we dove into a deep discussion.
Specs First, Vibes Second
John opened with the reality check every developer faces: "Vibe coding something de novo from a single prompt only works for the simple stuff, and you have a bad experience as soon as you go into the deeper water. The irony here is that vibe coders are rediscovering software engineering best practices — you start with a spec.”
Chris emphasized the point: "I personally ask Kilo Code to write its own plan first."
Tirumari (Kilo's support and community manager) added: "One programmer created SpecGram [ https://substack.com/redirect/1806a831-f3bd-497d-a318-44e6e2943d93?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ], a repo focused on spec-driven development that takes advantage of how customizable Kilo Code is."
John summed it up: "It sounds like your philosophy is: Okay, we're open source, so let's just open source this thing."
It’s true; we believe the community of builders knows best. This is why we take time to review dozens of issues [ https://substack.com/redirect/2aea1d76-8fbb-4143-967e-e5fd70750b58?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ], discussion threads [ https://substack.com/redirect/7ff5fcac-9b16-440f-8534-aa055b74cba4?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ], and community PRs [ https://substack.com/redirect/03c68d34-9bf4-4cba-8d9f-c47e01a3d8de?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] on a regular basis. Not to mention all the chatter on our Discord [ https://substack.com/redirect/9dedd79c-4046-42a0-8f14-6f8bb029307d?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]!
Cross-Model Critique Made Simple
The room had no shortage of ideas for our roadmap. There was abundant frustration with the standard cross-model workflows using the standard AI coding tools: "One of the things that excites me most about Kilo Code is that it looks like you're going to make it easier for me to use my own API keys to get different models to critique each other," said John. “It's one of the most valuable things, and right now it's a pain... If I'm coming from another app, I'm copy-pasting or pointing it at a file that might not have the whole context. It just sucks. So it sounds like you guys can make this a mode, right?"
“Yes!” confirmed Chris, after which he walked through the different modes and showed how you can install the modes marketplace [ https://substack.com/redirect/2f1fe57c-672c-4a73-8076-4b430d95c395?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ], which is full of community contributions. "You can make as many custom modes as you want. They can all have their own system prompts and tool access."
As Chris showed, the implementation is straightforward: "Create a new custom mode [ https://substack.com/redirect/dec63f98-301c-4282-9955-298dc73603d9?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] and link it with whichever provider you want to do the review."
As John saw it, "That's most of the solution right there."
Context Management That Actually Works
Another challenge from the room was about context rot: "I am constantly babysitting my big seven-phase.md file as it goes through one case at a time, having to clear context manually. Can I accomplish programmatic context clearing?"
Chris jumped in, explaining the orchestrator approach: "You start in orchestrator mode and say, 'Delegate code tasks for each phase of this plan.' When it's done, it only returns the information the parent needs." That way, the parent branch never gets polluted with the growing context streams.”
During the demo, this delegation happened in real-time. "Once it delegates into a new task, you can scroll back in history to review each task," Chris explained.
Visualizing Context Usage
The demo also sparked discussion about context window visualization. One member requested something like SpaceMonger for hard drives: "I want to see what's in this context and think, 'Oh, we don't need this. We don't need that.'"
Chris showed how Kilo Code already flags context usage: "When you hit 50% or more, we start flagging it, because that's when hallucination increases."
Building With Developers
The SPC forum reinforced something we believe deeply: the best tools emerge from real developer feedback, not boardroom feature lists. This is also the power of open source; when developers aren’t locked into a proprietary toolkit, when they can bring their own API keys and experiment with 400+ AI models, when you’re a Discord message away from their feedback and feature requests, you get a vibrant community you actually want to ship for.
SpecGram exists because someone needed spec-driven development and had the tools to create it. That's exactly why we built Kilo Code the way we did — and why conversations like this matter more than any polished demo.
We're not trying to guess what developers need. We're building alongside them.
Play our vibe-coded snake game [ https://substack.com/redirect/d4f4c049-a537-4467-853b-1f2fc10966e2?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] or explore the GitHub repo [ https://substack.com/redirect/85e92979-be46-4d46-ba21-48705b111447?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] to see how it all came together.
Your Turn
Join our community on Discord [ https://substack.com/redirect/a393b7c8-2536-49eb-8f1b-33ea1f0273a9?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] and follow our Github repo [ https://substack.com/redirect/b39e39f1-76c3-4b68-aca2-3e3e539b5e3e?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]. We’re nearing 10K stars! And psst, once we hit that milestone, we’re celebrating it by giving everyone $10 in Al model usage credits [ https://substack.com/redirect/e11c6815-f964-43a5-89e5-cf55407f4a72?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]!
Ready to try it yourself? Get started at kilocode.ai [ https://substack.com/redirect/691770f7-0df2-4d92-b9fb-506a59fc5bf3?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] and bring your team [ https://substack.com/redirect/9c8a7286-20e5-4546-a312-a77003958dcb?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] over!
Because the best AI coding tools aren't built in isolation — they're built in conversation with the developers who use them every day.

What happens when you take a solid AI coding model, make it free and fast, and put it in the hands of everyone who’s trying to build a software product?
You get a creativity explosion.
That’s exactly what’s happening with Grok Code Fast 1. In the last few days alone, Kilo Code has processed [ https://substack.com/redirect/daa0cc83-692c-4ed1-bf8a-fe5a6e5117c1?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] over 1 trillion tokens with this model:
That translates into thousands of side projects, client requests delivered, and new business ideas brought to life.
Why are people using Grok Code Fast 1 over Sonnet 4?
When we asked power users why they choose Grok over Sonnet, we uncovered an interesting pattern.
Many people said they use Grok because it’s fast.
But wait, what’s the point of being fast if you’re just outputting bad code faster?
That’s where an AI coding agent like Kilo Code comes into the picture.
Digging deeper, we found it's not about raw speed—it's about iteration cycles.
Imagine you have 2 minutes to build something using both Grok Code Fast 1 and Sonnet 4 with an AI coding agent like Kilo Code.
After 60 seconds with Grok:
Grok generates the code
Kilo Code reads it, runs it, shows the console output/errors, feeds that back into Grok
Grok takes the feedback and generates an improved version
Repeat steps 1-3 at least 4-5 times during the 40 seconds you have left
After 60 seconds with Sonnet:
 1) Still generating that “perfect” first attempt at a slower TPM (token-per-minute) rate, the iteration cycles are 3-5x longer.
It's like the startup world; being fast beats being perfect.
Here’s an image to help you visualize this:
What are people actually shipping?
We interviewed over 40 of Grok Code Fast 1 power users to find out what they're creating with the model. Here’s what they told us:
"I built an app for Indian consumers that's basically production-ready, thanks to Grok Fast."
"I created a Telegram bot with zero coding experience."
"I had ideas sitting around for years—some for over a decade—and finally brought them to life now that Grok is free."
"Built a Shopify app for e-commerce merchants."
"Knocked out a WordPress plugin in under a week."
Those people aren’t trying to build the next Facebook.
They're creating focused, practical apps that solve real problems for themselves, their clients and communities.
App extensions: Build it and they will come
I’ve noticed tons of people mentioning that they’re building extensions for major platforms (Chrome, Shopify, Telegram, etc.) which got me curious.
A few years ago, I did some research [ https://substack.com/redirect/e43d6c91-8c32-44e9-b951-81bf30c9813a?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] where I analyzed over 494 founder interviews, trying to find which acquisition channels consistently work for founders.
One channel stood out, where many of the founders interviewed essentially said, "I built this app, launched it, and users just showed up."
I called this channel app extension marketplaces.
An app extension is a plugin built for a major platform with millions of users. Think:
Shopify apps in the Shopify App Store [ https://substack.com/redirect/0ff18392-1294-4994-bcf9-2cebc3c4fbb1?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]
WordPress plugins in the WordPress Plugin Directory [ https://substack.com/redirect/b7647951-8d53-480f-8e17-4b635af1e9b2?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]
Chrome extensions in the Chrome Web Store [ https://substack.com/redirect/913f1310-7580-45f7-a3c3-5773be174418?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]
Kilo Code itself is an extension—we're on the VS Code Marketplace [ https://substack.com/redirect/cf8d848a-f264-4ae7-95ad-606aa59cec1e?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] (and now on JetBrains!)
Here's why this channel works: The marketing is done for you. Google Chrome, WordPress, and Microsoft have hundreds of millions of active users who are actively looking for solutions. Plus, these platforms promote their marketplaces heavily.
These app marketplaces function like mini search engines where people look for specific solutions—an ad blocker for Chrome, or a Git visualization tool.
More founders are catching on to this.: They realize extensions are way simpler to build than full-blown SaaS products. So those founders are focusing on cranking out products ("build it") and letting the marketplaces handle distribution ("they will come").
Fast & cheap & good AI models, combined with an AI coding agent help those people ship faster.
Your first idea probably won’t work
Up to 90% of startup ideas fail [ https://substack.com/redirect/ac0f6e81-ae22-4c5e-ae80-267651c468df?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ].
There's no magic formula to beat those odds. Markets shift, customer needs evolve, and game-changing competitors appear out of nowhere.
As a result, people are building. Building as much as you can and seeing what resonates.
Here’s what Pieter Levels, the world’s most famous bootstrapped founder, says about this:
Low-cost AI models let you build faster. Building faster means you can test more ideas and see what sticks.
You might be thinking: "But aren't cheaper AI models worse at writing code?"
The answer is yes, but that doesn’t matter. Let me explain.
Industry benchmarks show Grok Code 1 currently trails behind Sonnet [ https://substack.com/redirect/e9dd1733-88ee-4a5e-b545-ac66442ba0a8?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ].
But that doesn’t matter much because AI coding agents (like Kilo Code) can help transform low-cost AI models (like Grok) into iteration machines.
The bottom line
We discovered two counterintuitive insights from surveying our Grok Code Fast 1 users.
Most AI model benchmarks miss the bigger picture by focusing on isolated performance metrics.
Hopefully this gives you a different, more coherent perspective and a clear takeaway: Consider a fast, "good enough" model over a slower "perfect" one—especially when paired with the right tools.

subject: September 15, 2025: The Day the Industry Admitted AI Subscriptions Don't Work
body:
View this post on the web at https://blog.kilocode.ai/p/why-ai-subscriptions-cannot-work

Remember when we said flat-fee pricing for access to AI models can be summarized as: Painless now, feel the real pain later [ https://substack.com/redirect/7466bd9f-aff9-4b17-a89d-f4dbde25cb86?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]?
Well, today is "later" for Cursor and Kiro users. As of September 15, 2025, Cursor continues its tradition of arbitrarily rolling out changes that are worse for the community, and Kiro has also decided that it wants some of your cash now. Cue the surprised Pikachu memes.
What happened? In short:
Cursor
Rejigged "unlimited" Auto mode for individual Pro users to now be “competitively priced”
Switched the Teams plan from per-request pricing to variable token costs
Kiro
Raised their pricing again after already decreasing the number of requests from 3,000 to 650 4 weeks ago [ https://substack.com/redirect/47d93cab-2d36-4284-a725-bf0c0410f9d5?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]
Fully gave into ~vibe pricing~
Here’s why this matters.
"Competitive" Pricing That’s Significantly More Expensive Than the Competition’s
Cursor claims its auto mode will contribute to your included monthly usage at “competitive token rates [ https://substack.com/redirect/774a9184-ca9a-4a22-b6e3-734d89cfea6e?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ].” Translated from corporate speak, that means "You're now paying per token, just like everyone else."
In terms of numbers, here’s what “competitive” means in Cursor-land:
Input + cache write: $1.25 per 1M tokens
Output: $6.00 per 1M tokens
Cache read: $0.25 per 1M tokens
Meanwhile, here’s the pricing for Grok Code Fast 1 [ https://substack.com/redirect/40c806ca-5a29-4799-9efc-c2e4f990d6cf?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]:
Input: $0.20 per 1M tokens (6.25x cheaper than Cursor)
Output: $1.50 per 1M tokens (4x cheaper than Cursor)
Cached: $0.02 per 1M tokens (12.5x cheaper than Cursor)
More for Less
Cursor’s auto mode dynamically selects AI models based on availability and cost-efficiency, meaning it’ll give you whatever model is cheapest, not the one you want. Sure, it might save on fees, but at the cost of your control.
Imagine if Netflix said "unlimited streaming!" but randomly switched your 4K movie to 480p whenever their bandwidth costs got too high. That's auto mode.
None of that is “competitive.” Not the pricing nor the features.
Cursor Teams Plans Shift to Variable Pricing
Cursor's Teams pricing also changed [ https://substack.com/redirect/96369a13-8cdf-437f-98cc-9eb87e08b587?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] on September 15:
Before September 15:
250 Sonnet requests per month
Additional usage at $0.08 per request
After September 15:
$20 of agent usage per user
Ability to purchase additional usage
All usage is consumed at the publicly listed API prices of the underlying model + Cursor’s markup fee of $0.25 per million total tokens (Kilo doesn’t charge a markup on tokens for teams users)
Cursor explains the change:
“Using the same model, a single difficult prompt can consume an order of magnitude more tokens than a simple one.”
Tellingly, they themselves admit, “Fixed costs per request aren't suited to this new reality.” That's exactly why subscription pricing for AI never made sense in the first place.
Meanwhile at Kiro: "Vibes" Pricing
While Cursor realized they have to pull back on the unlimited promise, Kiro – the closed-source latecomer with the suspiciously familiar name (amazing what one letter can do!) – has decided it wants that cash and has introduced its own custom pricing model. The Amazon-backed tool decided to reinvent the wheel with something that’s, once again, willfully opaque. Here’re the terms they’ve introduced:
Spec requests are when you execute tasks within Kiro's structured development workflow
Vibe requests cover any agentic operation that does not involve spec requests
Easy, right? But dig a little deeper, and it gets funky. Just look at how they explain it [ https://substack.com/redirect/1bd69755-3ffe-489f-a98d-3ac652f6fc0f?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]:
We’ll give them the benefit of the doubt and assume they’re doing their best to give us some understanding, but this convoluted structure reminds us of the fine print in an insurance policy. Why not just, for example, charge what the usage costs?
Likewise, their overage pricing – $0.20/spec request or $0.04/vibe request – might sound reasonable until you realize you have no way to predict how many of each you'll need because all of this is based on average complexity. What does that entail, exactly?
Here’s the fundamental problem: proprietary units don't translate directly to tokens, making it difficult to compare costs across platforms. It's the same subscription trap Cursor fell into, just wrapped in different packaging, proving that being backed by Big Tech doesn't mean you understand the economics of AI [ https://substack.com/redirect/6640578d-4146-4ff1-b226-84319ae227f2?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] any better than the rest.
The Pattern Keeps Repeating
We’ve seen this same thing play out before:
The hook: "Unlimited AI coding for just $20/month!"
The adoption: Developers integrate it into their workflow
The reality check: Power users consume $1,000+ worth of compute daily
The squeeze: Introduce "rate limits," "usage pools," or "competitive pricing"
The backlash: "Why, as an active paying customer, didn't I get any e-mail from Cursor with clear explanation of upcoming changes"
The apology: "We didn't handle this pricing rollout well"
Three months ago, we predicted it [ https://substack.com/redirect/7466bd9f-aff9-4b17-a89d-f4dbde25cb86?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]. Then we watched Cursor’s June-July pricing disaster [ https://substack.com/redirect/c0dd6925-1715-4a1d-b555-e7e00590278c?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] unfold. Then Anthropic did it with Claude Code [ https://substack.com/redirect/32cb4ad6-754b-4724-8776-17942b2cef88?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ].
Anthropic, the company that makes Claude, realized it couldn’t sustainably offer unlimited, unthrottled access to their own models for a flat fee. If the creator and operator of the model can’t land this offer, how can any wrapper around their API do the same?
Simple: they can't. We’re not sure why Kiro’s trying a similar playbook.
We weren't being prophetic. We were just doing basic math. And developers are doing the math too [ https://substack.com/redirect/f903714f-b19d-4ecc-a30c-48fcef79aed9?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ].
The Bottom Line
September 15, 2025 marked another milestone in the AI coding subscription game.
Cursor’s users are learning what we've been saying for months: there's no sustainable way to offer unlimited access to expensive AI models at consumer price points.
The future isn't subscriptions with hidden limits and sudden changes. It isn’t arbitrary units based on vibes [ https://substack.com/redirect/51526cb0-c6f5-4d51-9f5a-0654650755d8?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] either.
It's transparent, usage-based pricing that respects both the economics of AI and the intelligence of developers.
That’s what we’re about at Kilo Code. Because when you align incentives properly, everyone wins:
You get the exact model you want
You pay only for what you use at no markup (our money comes from Teams [ https://substack.com/redirect/bc1c4b3e-d30c-4f50-ab9a-e1f74c933b50?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] and Enterprise [ https://substack.com/redirect/050a3252-326a-4d95-93c3-9a6d7d31c878?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] plans)
You can optimize costs [ https://substack.com/redirect/18353056-891f-4c5d-a692-a66427bb6c1f?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] in real-time
You never get surprised by a pricing change
Because being opaque with your developer community isn't just bad ethics – it's bad business.
Welcome to the honest side of AI coding. Your tokens are waiting, no subscription required. And we launched Autocomplete on September 4 [ https://substack.com/redirect/d55df552-7be9-41f7-a2ea-642cda2b0ec5?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]. It isn’t as good as Cursor’s yet but it will continue to improve this month and next.
P.S. To every Cursor or Kiro user reading this who's tired of the pricing gymnastics: we've got your back. Join ourDiscord [ https://substack.com/redirect/6ebe1b2c-eb59-4bf0-abbc-d5116b610e06?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] where you can even talk about competitors (yes, really). First $5 in credits on us (plus $20 more if you top up at least $5), no strings attached.

subject: Grok Code Bonanza: We Have Our Winners!
snippet: Last week we announced a Grok Code Bonanza where our users got the chance to show off what they've built using xAI's Grok Code Fast model (currently free through Kilo Code, but not for much
body:
View this post on the web at https://blog.kilocode.ai/p/grok-code-bonanza-we-have-our-winners

Last week we announced a Grok Code Bonanza [ https://substack.com/redirect/bc285eb2-7dff-498c-a1bd-bb516e2cfa49?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] where our users got the chance to show off what they’ve built using xAI’s Grok Code Fast model (currently free through Kilo Code, but not for much longer! [ https://substack.com/redirect/546cd297-4cea-43c8-92d9-da38e8c9e806?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]). We saw some very cool submissions [ https://substack.com/redirect/a66c7781-a41b-4192-9c76-e5d3ee644ff4?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ], and after some careful deliberation, we narrowed it down to our four winners!
Each winner built something that addressed a problem that they were personally dealing with and used their Kilo Code extension with Grok Code Fast to considerably speed up their process. It shouldn’t be a surprise, but we see many moments where talented and dedicated programmers tackle projects that would normally take them weeks or even months and reach their goals in a fraction of the time just by effectively utilizing AI. They’re still solving problems and creating solutions, but a coding assistant like Kilo Code has supercharged their efforts and we’re sharing some of these results here!
Join me as we step through these impressive projects! First up, one of our users and their team had been considering moving away from Wordpress over to Next.js;
A Complete Migration from WordPress to Next.js [ https://substack.com/redirect/7fbd5972-21f7-492c-a1fb-6af85d09e5fb?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]
Many of us know; WordPress can be…a lot. I remember my freelance days and a friend asked me to help his friends with a WordPress site they had. Cue some of the most frustrating two weeks I’ve ever experienced; I came out the other end like Robin Williams in Jumanji, frantically asking people what year it was.
This user told us that they had been deliberating on this task for months, but once they folded Kilo Code into their workflow and got started, they “did it in a week and added a cool feature to test the SEO of our website.”
The best part was the speed and accuracy with grok code. What was being thought about to do for months was done just in a week with grok code. All thanks to Kilo code team and definitely Grok code
I’ll be honest with you all, Younger Tirumari spent days messaging friends on Facebook to see if anyone had any insight on WordPress, hours googling questions, and even more hours scouring archived forums. I’m feeling a pang of jealousy here, but I’m mostly feeling proud for our first winner!
Speaking of scouring the internet, it sometimes feels like the internet has become so vast that finding what you’re looking for can prove pretty difficult. Even for those of us with honed Google-Fu [ https://substack.com/redirect/8a27dc2d-edf3-491b-b71f-c995ba3e72ef?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]. Our next winner had this problem with GitHub repositories, and decided to do something about it;
A GitHub Profile Explorer [ https://substack.com/redirect/5bb83cc2-76c0-4055-ac38-c89c1e25e6a2?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]
This user wanted to be able to easily track and analyze GitHub profiles at a glance, and so he built ghRadar [ https://substack.com/redirect/00c3ecc1-638b-4e11-abfd-08fcb56cad2b?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]! I’ll let him describe it in his own words;
It all started with a simple idea: what if analyzing GitHub repos and profiles could feel as easy as checking the weather? I didn’t want endless manual searching. I wanted a radar for GitHub — something that instantly shows you what’s happening inside any repo or profile.
This project took him only four days from conception to completion! As someone who’s taught several coding bootcamp courses (shout-out to The Last Mile [ https://substack.com/redirect/547ed47b-5d38-472a-b57b-567e7b3bf2e1?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] and Next Chapter [ https://substack.com/redirect/c45945ae-8cb9-4f6c-aa17-f9f952fc2ce6?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]) I had to make suree that students were familiar and comfortable with platforms like GitHub and GitLab. It was fundamental to their ability to find resources in the open-source space and appreciate their position in the community as a whole. I’ll be recommending this one to coding education folks for sure!
Now something I’ve always wanted to gain more experience in was mobile development. Our last two winners used Kilo Code and Grok to build themselves some mobile apps and once again it took them days to accomplish what could have been months of coding. One user wanted an iOS version of a popular Android app;
A Privacy-Oriented Period Tracker [ https://substack.com/redirect/4373086a-bc3f-4347-b7a3-de94a61b9f6c?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]
Our user described their problem as such;
I wanted a simple privacy friendly rhythm tracker for iOS that was like Periodical from Android. Since none existed that worked the way I wanted or didn't collect disturbing amounts of user data I used Grok code to help speed up building my own.
My mobile development friends have told me many a time of how difficult mobile development can really be; you’re not just designing for several browsers, you got multilple devices and OS’s and all sorts of new roadblocks to deal with. This programmer said;
The beauty is certainly how fast it was to make, if I wanted to remake it I doubt it would take longer than a couple days.
We love to hear it! Finally, last but not least, this winner knew what we all know -scheduling is hard. So they built something to make it easier;
A Cross-Platform Event Tracker [ https://substack.com/redirect/a149ea3d-fcc4-405c-b511-32af97449107?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]
Being able to design an app that works for you is honestly a dream of mine. Like being able to customize your car’s engine or hemming your own clothes. This user built a clean, no-frills event tracker that simply works, and had the following features;
Offline-first with persistent local storage,
Dashboard + Calendar view,
Search by title or date range,
Color-coded icons and countdowns
What was especially nice was how much Kilo and Grok really helped them out;
Grok helped me breeze through app structure, local data handling, and UI logic with almost zero debugging. Fast, efficient, and beginner-friendly.
[This is] Perfect for anyone who has a tight budget and wants to ship fast ⚡️ without backend complexity!
Thanks for the kind words, and please help me keep track of my social life!
Final Thoughts
Kilo Code is open-source and free, as we’re always saying. What’s great about that to me is how much this extension can completely change a programmer’s skillset and potential. Being able to code something you’ve always imagined is no longer a pipe dream; it’s a daily reality for our users, and we couldn’t be prouder!
Congratulations to our winners, you each win $100 in credits!! Thank you for using Kilo Code, and here’s to many more amazing projects!
As for you readers, make sure to join our Discord [ https://substack.com/redirect/253a5662-e50a-42d1-b79d-b9fc7452892a?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] to participate in future events, benefit from ocassional promotional offers, and show off your own work to our growing community!

body:
View this post on the web at https://blog.kilocode.ai/p/choosing-the-right-ai-coding-model

Since xAI’s Grok Code launched on August 26th, we've seen something remarkable: our users pushed through 1T tokens for Grok Code Fast alone [ https://substack.com/redirect/2827769d-9751-4f8f-9042-0a3172e37439?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]. That's more than double the usage any other AI coding tool had for this model.
Why? One user put it perfectly: "Grok Code Fast accounted for 72% of my requests over the last week. I still use Claude occasionally—and over that same week, Claude accounted for 90% of my cost. Grok is 25x cheaper per request and 17x cheaper per token than Sonnet 4. Need I say more?"
Using Kilo Code’s internal data and simulated costs of tokens for Grok Code Fast, we can see that even as the usage dwarfed all other models, the simulated cost was still significantly less than the cost of Claude Sonnet 4 over the same period.
And developers are using it for real life projects. One user told us about their usage in Kilo Code: "I've used it to create two fully-fledged backend apps from the ground up—from brainstorming, to architecting, developing, debugging, and deployment. I've used it to analyze and reverse-engineer one app in a language I don't code in. I've used it to translate an entire Go app to Python. It needs supervision, but it doesn't cease to amaze me."
This combination of being fast, cheap, and "good enough" hits a sweet spot.
A Paradigm Shift
What we're seeing might be the beginning of something bigger. xAI's Grok Code Fast could crack open the OpenAI-Anthropic duopoly [ https://substack.com/redirect/9db71dc5-304c-45d7-aeec-fd93b6381304?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] by bringing AI-assisted coding to developers who've been sitting on the sidelines. These price-conscious developers were waiting, watching, wondering if AI coding was worth the investment. Now they're jumping in and building those projects they've been putting off.
But also let’s be real. When we surveyed our users, 31% said they don't plan to use Grok Code beyond the promotional period (which ends in a week, so there’s still time to expense it [ https://substack.com/redirect/22f1f7b0-a25e-4489-8061-122bf87d03f2?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]). When we asked what they'd use instead, 32% mentioned open-source models like Qwen and Kimi, while 60% said they'd go back to premium models like Claude and GPT.
This tells us something important: there's no one-size-fits-all model for every coding job.
It’s Not Just The Model
Here's what many developers might miss: the model is just one part of the equation. The way you work with it is equally important. In Kilo Code, the agentic layer handles the back-and-forth, the context management, and the iteration cycles. This means even a "good enough" model can produce good results when properly orchestrated.
The Practical Test
So when our community kept asking "which model for what task?", we decided to show, not tell.
Chris, one of our engineers, ran an experiment. And by "experiment," we mean a totally unscientific one where he was just kinda making up the scores as he went—but hey, sometimes that's the best way to go about it! Same project (a to-do list app), 6 different models. He set up separate profiles in Kilo Code for each model—Sonnet 4, Grok Code Fast, Qwen 3 Coder, Nemotron, GLM, and Sonoma Dusk Alpha—and documented his experience: the speed, the quality, the surprises, and yes, some frustrations.
Check out Chris's video walkthrough at the top of this page to see the detailed comparison and his response while he tests each model.
The Bottom Line
Chris's results tell a clear story: Yes, Sonnet 4 delivered the best quality (9/10), but it also costs the most. Here's the thing though—models like Grok Code Fast and Qwen 3 Coder produced genuinely solid results (8/10 and 8.5/10) at a fraction of the cost. There are legitimate options at every price point, and even "good enough" models can produce impressive results when used correctly.
You can even use different models for different parts of your project. In Kilo Code, you can switch between models on the fly. Let Sonnet 4 design your architecture where quality matters most, then switch to Grok Code Fast or Qwen for rapid iteration and implementation.
Grok Code Fast is still free, but if you top up for the first time right now [ https://substack.com/redirect/0ef6ab5d-48d7-4ae6-aa76-b4d17ad26c0a?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ], you'll get a $20 bonus, enough to build with Grok Code Fast for a month (based on avg usage) or use 400+ other models.
Your Next Move
1. Try Grok Code Fast free this week (final days!)
2. Use Claude for architecture, Grok for implementation
3. Top up now = $20 bonus [ https://substack.com/redirect/0ef6ab5d-48d7-4ae6-aa76-b4d17ad26c0a?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ] (~1 month of Grok usage, offer only applies to first time top ups)
4. Already a paying user? Get your whole team shipping faster with Kilo for Teams [ https://substack.com/redirect/bc472a06-2a98-493f-8355-85fe184e5760?j=eyJ1IjoiNmhlanh6In0.ojXtL-J1WJBFG8trPR0HGAXjJj-msqi3Kvgf2nOsk4M ]
